title: The treatment entity moves to S2 while the legacy story holds it in P3, and the case side consumes TreatmentApproved which the event catalogue does not list for rwb-case
source: _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (tables treatment, timer, dp_treatment); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 18, 41, 42, 44; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 9 and 14; legacy story RWB-E2-004 sections 1, 3, 4 and 13
section: s1 Story; s2 Business rationale; s4 Flow; s11 Data; s12.4 Events consumed; s19 Out of scope
description: RWB-E2-004 built the treatment row, its repository, its service and its published interface inside P3 Case and workflow, with JOB-05 and the TimerScheduler port firing the plan timers. The target splits the capability three ways: Architecture v5 slide 41 and slide 18 give S2 rwb-treatment the treatments, the settlement and deed-in-lieu agreements and the plan timers in schema rwb_treatment; the Ownership Map gives `timer` to P3 with the ruling that the row is only the screen projection while the clock is a durable Temporal timer in CaseWorkflow and TimerDue and JOB-05 are retired; and the Temporal and Drools design puts the restructure stage and the cure-period wait in TreatmentWorkflow on rwb-treatment. The case side must therefore consume TreatmentApproved and PaymentMissed, yet Architecture v5 slide 42 lists only rwb-comms and rwb-payment as consumers of TreatmentApproved, and no source states which of the two services writes the plan timer, which one sets PLAN_RUNNING and PLAN_CURE_PERIOD, or which one publishes CaseStateChanged for the plan move. The legacy story's AC1 to AC14 name the treatment write, the timer write and the route move as one service's work, so every criterion of the split needs one stated seam.
evidence: ownership.json tables.treatment.owner = S2, basis 'Architecture v5 slide 41 (S2 owns treatments, contracts, settlement and deed-in-lieu agreements, plan timers) and slide 18 S2 DB line; TSD S2 v2 T3.1'; tables.timer.ruling 'timer stays with P3 as the screen projection behind GET /cases/{caseId}/timers, while the clock itself is a durable Temporal timer in CaseWorkflow; TimerDue and JOB-05 are retired', asm ASM-A6-tables-12; Architecture v5 slide 42 row '10 | TreatmentApproved | rwb-treatment | rwb.treatment.events.v1 | rwb-comms, rwb-payment'; slide 44 'JOB-05 Timer check every 5 min all durable timers (retired)'; Temporal and Drools design slide 14 note 'rwb-case forwards the event to the running stage child, TreatmentWorkflow on queue rwb-treatment'; RWB-E2-004 section 13 'Package. S2 package recovery.treatment.record for the treatment record; P3 package recovery.casewf.plan for the plan timer listener'.
legacy_ref: RWB-E2-004 (AC1, AC2, AC4 to AC9, AC11 to AC14; legacy sections 3, 4, 11, 13)
proposed: Confirm in the wave 2 architecture review that the treatment, its terms and its approval are S2's and never written in rwb_case, that rwb-case consumes rwb.treatment.TreatmentApproved.v1 and rwb.payment.PaymentMissed.v1 and holds the case route state, the timer projection and the durable plan timer in CaseWorkflow, and add rwb-case to the consumer list of TreatmentApproved in the event catalogue so the subscription is contractual.

title: The 01:30 treatment extract has no owner in the target and its DP04 read path and freshness element are not in the Ownership Map
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 37, 41 and 44; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (tables dp_treatment, lake_copy_watermark, data_product); legacy story RWB-E2-004 sections 4, 5 and 12
section: s4 Flow; s5 Exception paths X7; s11 Data; s12.2 REST operations consumed; s19 Out of scope
description: The legacy story owns the extract step: JOB-15 Reporting extract at 01:30 reads changed treatments through TreatmentRecords.changedSince, writes the DP04 treatment data product, and shows the previous business date with MSG-P1-001 when it fails. In the target the data lake is removed (DP-17; ADR-018) and the job map gives JOB-15 to rwb-reporting at 01:30 with an Airflow trigger and no data lake, while the Ownership Map gives dp_treatment to P1 rwb-source-data as a dated copy built from events. No source says who owns the treatment extract step, which service serves the DP04 treatment rows, or what path and what freshness element the case side reads for AC3 and AC10; the Ownership Map API section carries no data-product operation at all, and the lake_copy_watermark ruling records that the only legacy table tied to the removed lake is dropped rather than replaced.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 44 'JOB-15 | Reporting extract | 01:30 | rwb-reporting | Airflow trigger (no data lake)'; slide 37 and DP-17 'no data lake connection'; ownership.json tables.dp_treatment.owner = P1 with ruling 'The live treatment and guarantee records stay with S2 and S3; the dated DP04 copies stay with P1 as the data engine (TSD P1 v3), built from events and read-only for reporting', asm ASM-A6-tables-14; tables.lake_copy_watermark.ruling 'lake_copy_watermark is a P1 legacy table with no target: the data lake is removed'; RWB-E2-004 section 4 step 10 'JOB-15 Reporting extract: each night reads changed treatments through TreatmentRecords.changedSince(...) and writes the treatment data product (DP04)'; section 12 'JOB-15 Reporting extract (nightly 01:30)' as a P3 job; the api section of ownership.json has no data-product row.
proposed: Record the owner of the treatment extract as P9 rwb-reporting on JOB-15 with the DP04 copy in rwb_source_data, publish the case-facing read GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/DP04/records with its freshness element in the Ownership Map and the P1 API file, and state in the event catalogue that the copy is built from the treatment events.

title: No source fixes the plan-timer fields, types or required flags of the timers answer behind GET /cases/{caseId}/timers
source: _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (api 'GET /cases/{caseId}/timers', tables timer); Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5 TSD P3 v3 T3.1 and T3.2; legacy story RWB-E2-004 sections 11 and 12
section: s11 Data; s12.1 REST operations provided; s13 Solution plan (Database)
description: The ruling keeps the `timer` row as the projection behind the timers operation and the plan timers carry `treatment_id` (DF-WRK-042), with the timer types INSTALLMENT_DUE and CURE_PERIOD already present in LOV-TIMER. What no source gives is the answer shape: whether the timers resource returns `treatmentId`, whether a plan timer carries the rule ID and the package version it was created under, whether `expiresAt` is a zone-qualified instant or a local date-time, and which of these properties are required. TSD P3 v3 names the table columns but not the REST properties, the Ownership Map names the operation but not its schema, and the legacy story's own contract section described the table and the TimerScheduler port rather than the JSON shape. The app, contract and test stories of this key and the wave 2 harness all read the same answer, so the shape has to be fixed once.
evidence: ownership.json tables.timer.ruling 'timer stays with P3 as the screen projection behind GET /cases/{caseId}/timers'; api 'GET /cases/{caseId}/timers' owner P3 with no response shape; TSD P3 v3 T3.1 columns DF-WRK-027 to DF-WRK-036, DF-WRK-042 to DF-WRK-044 and T3.2 'LOV-TIMER | SERVICE_LEVEL, NOTICE_PERIOD, CURE_PERIOD, PRESCRIPTION, HEARING_DEADLINE, OFFER_VALIDITY, HOLDING_AGE, CLAIM_DEADLINE, INSTALLMENT_DUE'; RWB-E2-004 section 12 'GET /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}/timers (P3) returns Timer[]' with no field list.
legacy_ref: RWB-E2-004 (AC2, AC12, AC14; legacy section 11 and 12)
proposed: Fix the plan-timer properties in the RWB-P3-E2004-CON baseline review with the timer owner (RWB-P3-E1028-CON) and the harness: treatmentId, timerType, startedAt, expiresAt, warnAt, paused and status, all optional within major version 1, with expiresAt as an offset date-time, and record them in the rwb-case OpenAPI file.

title: No source gives the alert values for the plan-timer projection, the subscription lag, the DP04 freshness or the exception-queue count
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 28 and 44; legacy story RWB-E2-004 sections 5 and 13; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 R7.2 s17
section: s11 Data; s13 Solution plan (Alert mapping); s14 Validation and messages
description: The deployment alerts on the projection lag between arming a plan timer and reading its row, on the lag of the two subscriptions, on the `.dlt` count, on the exception-queue count of refused plan steps and on the freshness of the DP04 treatment product, but no source gives a threshold, a window or a band. The legacy story names only a five-minute timer check that the target retires and a consumer retry limit of 3; the FSD and TSD P3 give no operational value, and the architecture extract names the alert as a capability without a number. Every value therefore has to be a values-file entry with a provisional default, and the runbook entry each alert links has to state that the value is provisional.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 44 'JOB-21 Stuck workflow scan | every 5 min | platform | visibility query + alert' with no threshold; slide 28 'stops at once (no retry); stuck-case alert' with no value; RWB-E2-004 section 5 X6 'retries the event 3 times' and section 13 'Event consumer retry limit 3 (NFR-026)' as the only numeric operational value; no threshold appears in FSD P3 v4, TSD P3 v3 or the Ownership Map.
proposed: Set the values in the rwb-case values files as provisional defaults, confirm them at UAT with the service owner and the platform observability owner, and record the agreed values in the runbook entry each alert links.
